1.mascotDialogue: An arrow in a directed graph means exactly one thing — you can go this way. That's it. Says nothin' at all about whether you can come on back.

2.mascotDialogue: Line 8 sets exactly one cell in the matrix. A directed edge only ever writes adjacency[u][v] — never touches adjacency[v][u], not once.

3.mascotDialogue: Every arrowhead points just one way here. This particular loop happens to form a cycle, sure, but each edge is still, on its own, one-directional.

4.mascotDialogue: This right here's the single most common directed-graph mistake — treatin' a one-way arrow like it secretly goes both ways. It don't. The visual only ever draws the direction you actually set.
